title: The engineering design process
examples: What is the first step when designing something?
How do engineers test their ideas?
Can you give an example of improving a design?

explain.say: Today we are learning the engineering design process. This helps us solve problems in the real world.
First, you must clearly define the problem. You need to know exactly what you are trying to solve. For example, if your books are too heavy, that is your problem.

draw.text: Define the Problem: What is wrong?

explain.say: Next, you must brainstorm many possible ideas. Do not judge any idea right away. For instance, you could use a backpack or a wheelbarrow.
After choosing an idea, you build a prototype. A prototype is an early working model of your design. For example, you might build a small cardboard model of the carrier.
Then, you must test your prototype carefully. You need to see if it actually solves the problem. For example, you test the cardboard carrier by filling it with books.
Finally, you use the test results to improve your design. If it breaks, you learn from that. For example, you might make the handles stronger next time.

faq.a: Engineers build prototypes to see if their idea actually works. It helps them find problems early before building the final product.
asks: What is the purpose of a model?
Why do we make a first version?

faq.q: Do I have to improve my design every time?
faq.a: No, but you should always check if improvements are needed. The process is about making the best possible solution.

faq.q: What is the difference between an idea and a prototype?
faq.a: An idea is just a thought or sketch. A prototype is a physical, working model of that idea.
asks: Are ideas and models the same?
Can I build something from just an idea?

faq.q: Which step comes right before testing?
faq.a: The step right before testing is building the prototype. You must build something physical to test it.
asks: What do I do before testing?

faq.q: If the first test fails, do I start over?
faq.a: No, you do not start completely over. You use the failure to guide your improvements for the next version.
asks: How do I fix a bad test result?

facts: The process is cyclical, meaning you repeat steps.
Defining the problem is the most crucial first step.
A prototype is a working model, not the final product.
Testing reveals weaknesses that need improvement.

quiz.say: A student wants to design a better pencil case. They first sketch three different designs. Which step are they currently in?
quiz.why: Sketching multiple options is part of brainstorming many ideas.

wrong.0: Building happens after you have chosen the best idea to model.
wrong.1: Testing happens after the model has been built and is ready to use.
wrong.3: This step asks what the current problem is, not how to solve it.

quiz.say: After building a small model of a bridge, the students find it collapses under weight. What should they do next?
quiz.why: A failure in testing directly tells you what needs to be improved.

wrong.0: You should first try to fix the current idea before abandoning it.
wrong.1: You must fix the weakness found during testing first.
wrong.3: The original problem (carrying weight) is still the same.

quiz.say: A student is trying to design a better water bottle. They write down: 'The bottle leaks when I put it in my bag.' This statement belongs to which stage?
quiz.why: Stating exactly what is wrong or what the goal is belongs here.

wrong.0: Improvement happens after you have already tested and found the leak.
wrong.2: A prototype is a physical object, not a written statement of the problem.
wrong.3: Testing is the action of checking the bottle, not writing about the leak.
